question.leadin: This ruler founded the Achaemenid [ah-KEE-men-id] Empire, which successfully grew by supporting local rulers as satraps and respecting local customs.
question.text: Name this "Great" Persian ruler of the sixth century BCE who ended the Babylonian Captivity.
question.clue: This son of Persis seized the city of Sardis after defeating the Lydian king, Croesus.

swap.text: In the Battles of Issus and Gaugamela, Alexander defeated Darius III, the ruler of this large empire centered on modern-day Iran.
swap.answerHtml: the First Persian Empire [or the Achaemenid Empire, or Xšāça]
swap.clue: King Psamtik III was defeated at the battle of Pelesium near the Nile Delta by a ruler of this empire named Cambyses II.

question.text: On Carter's last day in office, the signing of the Algiers Accords ended an event in this country. During that "hostage crisis" in this country, supporters of Ayatollah Khomeini invaded its U.S. embassy.
question.answerHtml: Iran [or Persia or Islamic Republic of Iran or IRI or Jomhuri-ye Eslâmi-ye Irân]
question.clue: This country created a literacy corps as part of its White Revolution.

swap.leadin: This empire was home to the first large-scale postal service, and the Behistun (bee-HIS-toon) inscription details the deeds of its ruler Darius the Great.
swap.text: Name this empire or the modern-day country sometimes equated with it. Shah Reza Pahlavi celebrated the 2500-year anniversary of the foundation of this empire.
swap.clue: One ruler of this empire famously ordered the ocean to be whipped.

question.text: The defenders of Edessa hung a squealing pig to frighten away an elephant used by this empire's Khosrau I (KUZ-rao the first). This longest-lasting Persian dynasty rivaled the Byzantines in the Middle East.
question.answerHtml: Sassanian Empire [or Sassanid Empire; or Sassanian Dynasty; or Sassanid Dynasty; or Eranshahr]
question.clue: The Byzantines fought a series of wars with this empire. Shapur the Great was one ruler of this empire. It was the final, non-Islamic dynasty to rule over all of Persia.

swap.text: The tyrant Aristagoras of Miletus led the Ionian Revolt against this ruler. The thirty-six satraps were established by this Persian ruler, whose forces invading Greece were defeated at Marathon.
swap.clue: This leader of an expedition against the Scythians divided his empire into twenty satrapies, and he built a noted network of roads.

question.text: According to the Chronicle of Early Kings, Sargon defeated an attempted invasion by four "great" generals from this polity, which was led by the King of Awan.
question.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

swap.text: After Roman triumvirate Crassus tried to invade this empire and failed, his was head was cut off and filled with molten gold in reference to his famous wealth.
swap.clue: An early use of the word "philhellene" , meaning "lover of the Greeks," was on the coins of this empire's Mithridates I , who was descended from the 3rd-century BC founder after whom this empire is sometimes named.

question.text: One of Alexander's successors was this general, who founded a namesake empire which ruled the Levant, Anatolia, and Mesopotamia under kings like Antiochus Epiphanes.
question.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

swap.text: This non-Persian empire of Iran was conquered by Cyrus the Great before he went on to conquer Lydia and Babylon, aided by a defector from this empire, Harpagus. Its last king was Astyages and its capital was Ecbatana.
swap.clue: As a result of a battle at the Halys River, that waterway was declared its border with Lydia.

question.text: Abu Bakr's military endeavors included sending Khalid ibn al-Walid to campaign against this empire. Its last emperor Yazdegerd III was defeated by al-Walid at the Battle of Qadisiyyah.
question.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

swap.leadin: One account says this ruler died while fighting Queen Tomyris and her Massagetae people.
swap.text: Name this ruler, whose son and successor was Cambyses II. He defeated the Babylonians at the battle of Opis and his Edict of Restoration ended the Israelites' Babylonian captivity.
swap.answerHtml: Cyrus II [accept Cyrus the Great or Cyrus the Elder]
swap.clue: This man defeated Nabonidus at the Battle of the Opis and bested Croesus at the Battle of Thymbra to conquer the Lydian Empire.

question.leadin: Heleen Sancisi-Weerdenburg argued that historians relied exclusively on Greek sources on this empire and that there was no solid evidence of its actual existence.
question.text: Name these people who, according to Herodotus, built the capital of Ecbatana and were last ruled by Astyages before his Persian grandson overthrew him around 550 BC.
question.clue: Early kings of these people included Deioces and Phraortes.

swap.text: The last Median ruler, Astyages, was overthrown by this grandson of his, who founded the Achaemenid Empire. He also allowed the Jews to return home after he conquered Babylon, and proclaimed an early charter of rights.
swap.answer: Cyrus the Great or Cyrus II
swap.clue: Indeed, he did overthrow Astyages in a rebellion against the Medes, and his Edict of Restoration gave the Jews permission to return to their homeland.

question.leadin: On the Letoon ("LET-oh-on") stele, the inscription in this language explicitly calls Pixodarus satrap of Caria and Lycia, rather than just Lycia in the Greek and Lycian versions.
question.text: Name this major administrative language in the Achaemenid bureaucracy. This Northwest Semitic language was also used in letters by Arshama, satrap of Egypt.
question.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

swap.text: During his rise to power, Septimius Severus defeated Pescennius Niger at this place in Turkey. In a 333 BC battle at this location, Alexander the Great defeated Darius III, setting up their final clash at Gaugamela.
swap.clue: In addition to that defeat of Pescennius Niger, this was the site of a 1266 battle at which King Hethum I of Armenia was defeated by Baibars.

question.leadin: Name these things about the Parthian Empire.
question.text: A man of this name fought a war against Izates and perhaps codified the Avesta as part of an Iranian Revival. The sixth and last Parthian king of this name faced trouble from the Sassanid Adrashir I.
question.clue: Septimus Severus defeated the fifth Parthian emperor with this name. The sixth emperor of this name would be defeated by the Sassanids in the early third century CE.

swap.text: The first ruler of this name faced Inaros's revolt. The second Persian king of this name lost Egypt around the time of a revolt by his brother Cyrus the Younger, and later waged an unsuccessful 370s BCE campaign against Nectanebo I.
swap.answerHtml: Artaxerxes [or Artaxšaçā; accept Artaxerxes I or II; prompt on Arses or Arsaces by asking “what was his regnal name?”; reject “Xerxes” or “Ahasuerus”]
swap.clue: The first one was referred to as "the Long Handed" and ascended to the throne by killing Artabanus, who'd killed his father.

question.text: The namesake of the dynasty, Sassan, was a priest of this Persian religion that worshipped Ahura Mazda and became the Sassanid state religion.
question.clue: This chief religion sponsored by the Indo-Parthians and Parthians. Today, practitioners of this religion in India are called Parsees.

swap.text: In this document, Darius I told of how he overthrew the deceitful magus Gaumata, who had allegedly briefly ruled the empire while pretending to be Cambyses's brother Bardiya.
swap.clue: This document justifies the position of the ruler who ordered it created by claiming that he saved the kingdom from the possibly fictional usurper Gaumata.
